digest.component_or_area: reconciler vendor adapter seam / jira family backend architecture
propositions: `TicketTransport` protocol declares six members but the reconciler core actually calls twenty-one distinct transport members, with twelve absent from the DC adapter and undeclared on any Protocol, causing silent operational failures and occasional runtime crashes despite passing contract suite and unit tests.

ADR 0035 claims the backend contract suite certifies adapter completeness, but this claim is conditional on port completeness and static typing; an unannotated `client` parameter makes gaps invisible to type checkers, as proven by comparing `client: Any`, unannotated, and `client: TicketTransport` signatures.

`RemoteRef.instance` is presented in the decision as a deployment-distinguishing mechanism but is never constructed in production code (only in test helpers), so the shared-jira-channel provenance decision lacks the field needed to implement it.

ADR 0035 contains four stale falsified assertions that a later backend landed first: the first real second backend is out of scope appears in diagram comment, prose, Decision item 6, and Consequences section, but Jira Data Center landed ahead of the GitHub adapter.

The Jira family seam is built via dependency inversion on location-pinned modules (adf.py, outbound_fields.py, comment_limits.py) rather than relocation, deferring Phase 2 architectural reorganization and creating a non-obvious contract boundary.

DC read-only EOL date is 28 March 2029, making this a deliberately time-boxed investment for self-hosted clients where the durable asset is the family seam architecture rather than the DC adapter implementation itself.
